claim: Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) is the third cause of death among cancer patients.
source: Colorectal cancer (CRC), the third cause of death among cancer patients, is a highly heterogeneous disease, with a slow initial progression that favors the accumulation of mutations leading to a complex phenotype.
evidence: This is a statement presented in the introduction without specific citation, drawing on established medical knowledge.

claim: CRC is a highly heterogeneous disease with slow initial progression that favors accumulation of mutations leading to a complex phenotype.
source: Colorectal cancer (CRC), the third cause of death among cancer patients, is a highly heterogeneous disease, with a slow initial progression that favors the accumulation of mutations leading to a complex phenotype.
evidence: This is a general characterization of CRC based on established scientific understanding.

claim: Differences exist both between and within tumors of the same cancer type and are a major hurdle towards proper treatment selection and developing more targeted therapies.
source: Differences that exist both between and within tumors of the same cancer type are a major hurdle towards proper treatment selection and for developing more targeted therapies.
evidence: This is a general statement about tumor heterogeneity based on established knowledge in oncology.

claim: The TNM staging system constitutes the gold standard for diagnosis and prognosis of CRC.
source: The systematization of clinical and histopathological parameters led to the definition of current TNM staging system (Amin, 2017), which presently constitutes the gold standard for diagnosis and prognosis.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Amin, 2017.

claim: High throughput molecular technologies led to the appearance of molecular taxonomies categorizing tumors into subgroups sharing common molecular traits.
source: The development of high throughput molecular technologies brought a novel perspective and set the stage for the appearance of molecular taxonomies categorizing the tumors into subgroups sharing common molecular traits (Perez-Villamil et al., 2012; Budinska et al., 2013; Marisa et al., 2013; De Sousa E Melo et al., 2013; Sadanandam et al., 2013; Roepman et al., 2014) with consensus molecular subtypes (CMS)(Guinney et al., 2015) representing their common denominator.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies that developed molecular taxonomies.

claim: Consensus molecular subtypes (CMS) represent the common denominator of various molecular taxonomies of CRC.
source: The development of high throughput molecular technologies brought a novel perspective and set the stage for the appearance of molecular taxonomies categorizing the tumors into subgroups sharing common molecular traits (Perez-Villamil et al., 2012; Budinska et al., 2013; Marisa et al., 2013; De Sousa E Melo et al., 2013; Sadanandam et al., 2013; Roepman et al., 2014) with consensus molecular subtypes (CMS)(Guinney et al., 2015) representing their common denominator.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guinney et al., 2015, which established the CMS classification.

claim: Single-cell sequencing refined the CMS classes by adding two intrinsic epithelial subtypes (iCMS2/3).
source: While these studies were based on whole-tumor (bulk) gene expression data, the developments in single-cell sequencing further refined the CMS classes adding two intrinsic epithelial subtypes (iCMS2/3) to the picture (Joanito et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Joanito et al., 2022.

claim: Whole transcriptome expression profiling of tissue sections represents a weighted mean of contributions of each cell type, driven by the most abundant ones.
source: Whole transcriptome expression profiling of tissue sections is generally performed on RNA extracted from regions of interest covering diverse cell collections. By consequence, the expression levels associated with various transcripts represent, in the end, a weighted mean of contributions of each cell type, being driven by the most abundant ones.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the nature of bulk RNA sequencing.

claim: Signals from less abundant cell types are reduced or silenced in whole transcriptome profiling and are therefore overlooked.
source: The signals from less abundant cell types are reduced or even silenced and are, therefore, overlooked.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of bulk sequencing methodology.

claim: Jass, 2007 identified several morphological features associated with five molecular groups of CRC.
source: The importance of a morphological perspective on the molecular classification has been acknowledged from the beginning, Jass, 2007 already identifying several morphological features associated with the five groups proposed (e.g. serration, mucinous and poor differentiation were highly present in two of the five groups), but also noted that these features were not sufficient for predicting the groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jass, 2007.

claim: Morphological features alone were not sufficient for predicting molecular groups in Jass, 2007.
source: The importance of a morphological perspective on the molecular classification has been acknowledged from the beginning, Jass, 2007 already identifying several morphological features associated with the five groups proposed (e.g. serration, mucinous and poor differentiation were highly present in two of the five groups), but also noted that these features were not sufficient for predicting the groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jass, 2007.

claim: Budinska et al., 2013 proposed six morphological patterns (morphotypes) as major histological descriptors strongly associated with five molecular subtypes.
source: Later, Budinska et al., 2013 proposed six morphological patterns (morphotypes) as major histological descriptors and showed that a two-tier histological score is strongly associated with the five molecular subtypes identified.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Budinska et al., 2013.

claim: A data-driven image-based classifier for molecular subtypes selected morphological motifs similar to those identified by Budinska et al., 2013.
source: Interestingly, a pure data-driven image-based classifier for the same molecular subtypes resulted in selecting remarkably similar morphological motifs (Budinska et al., 2016; Popovici et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Budinska et al., 2016 and Popovici et al., 2017.

claim: Müller et al., 2016 reviewed the TCGA and CMS subtypes and their links with morphological aspects, notably the serrated phenotype.
source: Müller et al., 2016 reviewed the TCGA and CMS subtypes and their links with some morphological aspects, most notably the serrated phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Müller et al., 2016.

claim: Gene expression profile may depend on the tumor region sampled for RNA extraction.
source: These links between tumor morphology and molecular features also imply that the gene expression profile may depend on the tumor region sampled for RNA extraction.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the observation that morphology and molecular features are linked.

claim: Sensitivity of gene-based classifiers to tumor sampling raised concerns regarding the stability of consensus molecular subtypes.
source: The sensitivity of gene-based classifiers to tumor sampling raised concerns regarding the stability of consensus molecular subtypes (Dunne et al., 2016) and may partially explain the low proportion of biomarkers that reach clinical relevance (Stewart et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dunne et al., 2016 and Stewart et al., 2017.

claim: The study profiled 202 tumor regions from 111 stage II-IV CRCs by whole-transcriptome microarrays.
source: Whole-transcriptome profiling by microarrays of 202 tumor regions (morphotypes, tumor-adjacent normal tissue, supportive stroma, and matched whole tumors) from 111 stage II-IV CRCs identified morphotype-specific gene expression profiles and molecular programs and differences in their cellular buildup.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental design and data collection.

claim: The study identified morphotype-specific gene expression profiles and molecular programs.
source: Whole-transcriptome profiling by microarrays of 202 tumor regions (morphotypes, tumor-adjacent normal tissue, supportive stroma, and matched whole tumors) from 111 stage II-IV CRCs identified morphotype-specific gene expression profiles and molecular programs and differences in their cellular buildup.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: The proportion of cell types (fibroblasts, epithelial and immune cells) and differentiation of epithelial cells were the main drivers of disparities between morphotypes.
source: The proportion of cell types (fibroblasts, epithelial and immune cells) and differentiation of epithelial cells were the main drivers of the observed disparities with activation of EMT and TNF-α signaling in contrast to MYC and E2F targets signaling, defining major gradients of changes at molecular level.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of the data.

claim: Activation of EMT and TNF-α signaling in contrast to MYC and E2F targets signaling define major gradients of changes at molecular level between morphotypes.
source: The proportion of cell types (fibroblasts, epithelial and immune cells) and differentiation of epithelial cells were the main drivers of the observed disparities with activation of EMT and TNF-α signaling in contrast to MYC and E2F targets signaling, defining major gradients of changes at molecular level.
evidence: This is a finding based on pathway analysis of the expression data.

claim: Most gene expression-based classifiers, prognostic and predictive signatures exhibited important morphotype-dependent variability within same tumor sections.
source: Several gene expression-based (including single-cell) classifiers, prognostic and predictive signatures were examined to study their behavior across morphotypes. Most exhibited important morphotype-dependent variability within same tumor sections, with regional predictions often contradicting the whole-tumor classification.
evidence: This is a finding from applying existing classifiers to the morphotype data.

claim: Regional predictions from gene expression-based classifiers often contradicted the whole-tumor classification.
source: Several gene expression-based (including single-cell) classifiers, prognostic and predictive signatures were examined to study their behavior across morphotypes. Most exhibited important morphotype-dependent variability within same tumor sections, with regional predictions often contradicting the whole-tumor classification.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing regional and whole-tumor predictions.

claim: Morphotype-based tumor sampling allows detection of molecular features that would otherwise be distilled in whole tumor profile while maintaining histopathology context.
source: The results show that morphotype-based tumor sampling allows the detection of molecular features that would otherwise be distilled in whole tumor profile, while maintaining histopathology context for their interpretation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Morphotype-based sampling represents a practical approach at improving the reproducibility of expression profiling and gene-based classifiers.
source: This represents a practical approach at improving the reproducibility of expression profiling and, by consequence, of gene-based classifiers.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the practical implications of the study.

claim: From n=111 unique cases of primary CRC tumors, n=202 regions were macrodissected.
source: From n=111 unique cases of primary CRC tumors (stages: II: 59, III:32, IV:20), n=202 regions were macrodissected representing either tumor morphological regions (n=149), tumor-adjacent normal tissue (NR, n=17), supportive stroma (ST, n=8), or whole tumor (n=28), respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sample collection.

claim: Among the tumor morphological regions, n=126 'core samples' were identified based on 'morphological purity' (at least 80% of a unique morphological pattern).
source: Among the tumor morphological regions, n=126 'core samples' were identified based on 'morphological purity', indicating regions containing at least 80% of a unique morphological pattern.
evidence: This describes the criteria for selecting core samples.

claim: The only statistically significant associations found were between MU or TB and grade 3 tumors, and SE and lower grade tumors (p=0.019).
source: The only statistically significant associations found were between MU or TB and grade 3 tumors, and SE and lower grade tumors (p=0.019, Supplementary file 2), respectively.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the analysis of clinical parameters.

claim: ESTIMATE indicated high stromal content for ST, DE, and MU morphotypes.
source: The results from ESTIMATE indicated, as expected, a high stromal content for ST, DE, and MU and a high epithelial tumor cell content for normal region and TB and SE morphotypes, respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from computational deconvolution analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ESTIMATE indicated high epithelial tumor cell content for normal region and TB and SE morphotypes.
source: The results from ESTIMATE indicated, as expected, a high stromal content for ST, DE, and MU and a high epithelial tumor cell content for normal region and TB and SE morphotypes, respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from computational deconvolution analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ST, DE, and MU were enriched in endothelial cells, CAFs and immune cells according to Isella signatures.
source: This agreed with the (stroma-related) 'Isella signatures' (Isella et al., 2015) where ST, DE, and MU were enriched in endothelial cells, CAFs and immune cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis using Isella signatures, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Signatures of top of the normal colon crypt cells and colon differentiated epithelial cells were enriched solely in NR regions.
source: When investigating the categories of epithelial cells, the signatures of top of the normal colon crypt cells (Kosinski et al., 2007) and colon differentiated epithelial cells (Merlos-Suárez et al., 2011) were enriched solely in NR regions, while DE, MU, CT, SE, and TB were depleted in these cell types (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2B, supported by citations.

claim: DE, MU, CT, SE, and TB were depleted in signatures of top of the normal colon crypt cells and colon differentiated epithelial cells.
source: When investigating the categories of epithelial cells, the signatures of top of the normal colon crypt cells (Kosinski et al., 2007) and colon differentiated epithelial cells (Merlos-Suárez et al., 2011) were enriched solely in NR regions, while DE, MU, CT, SE, and TB were depleted in these cell types (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MU, CT, PP, and TB regions expressed genes specific for the basal crypt cells.
source: On the other hand, MU, CT, PP, and TB regions expressed genes specific for the basal crypt cells (Kosinski et al., 2007) and ST, DE, and MU were enriched in signatures of intestinal stem cells.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis, supported by citation.

claim: ST, DE, and MU were enriched in signatures of intestinal stem cells.
source: On the other hand, MU, CT, PP, and TB regions expressed genes specific for the basal crypt cells (Kosinski et al., 2007) and ST, DE, and MU were enriched in signatures of intestinal stem cells.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: quanTIseq revealed that all tumor morphotypes were enriched in M1 macrophages with maximal presence in MU and DE.
source: quanTIseq revealed that all tumor morphotypes were enriched in M1 macrophages (with maximal presence in MU and DE), while M2 macrophages, NK cells and myeloid dendritic cells where highly present in supporting stroma and tumor-adjacent normal regions (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from immune cell deconvolution analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: M2 macrophages, NK cells and myeloid dendritic cells were highly present in supporting stroma and tumor-adjacent normal regions.
source: quanTIseq revealed that all tumor morphotypes were enriched in M1 macrophages (with maximal presence in MU and DE), while M2 macrophages, NK cells and myeloid dendritic cells where highly present in supporting stroma and tumor-adjacent normal regions (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from immune cell deconvolution analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TB morphotype had the lowest scores for regulatory T cells (TREGs) and B cells.
source: Additionally, TB morphotype had the lowest scores for regulatory T cells (TREGs) and B cells.
evidence: This is a finding from immune cell deconvolution analysis.

claim: ST, MU, and DE had high GSEA scores of most of the CAFs subpopulations.
source: Interestingly, the morphotypes differed in the signatures of CAFs subpopulations (Figure 2D). ST, MU, and DE had high GSEA scores of most of the CAFs subpopulations, while the rest (CT, PP, SE, and TB) had mostly negative scores, indicative of depletion of corresponding cell types.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis of CAF signatures shown in Figure 2D.

claim: CT, PP, SE, and TB had mostly negative scores for CAFs subpopulations, indicative of depletion of corresponding cell types.
source: Interestingly, the morphotypes differed in the signatures of CAFs subpopulations (Figure 2D). ST, MU, and DE had high GSEA scores of most of the CAFs subpopulations, while the rest (CT, PP, SE, and TB) had mostly negative scores, indicative of depletion of corresponding cell types.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis of CAF signatures shown in Figure 2D.

claim: DE and MU were most strongly enriched in signatures of ECM-myCAF S1 and wound-healing myCAF S1 populations.
source: DE and MU were most strongly enriched in signatures of ECM-myCAF S1 – associated with immunosuppressive microenvironment and pro-metastatic functions (Kieffer et al., 2020) – and wound-healing myCAF S1 populations, while the adjacent stroma mainly showed signatures of normal fibroblasts, detox-iCAF S1 and IL-iCAF S1 populations, both characterized by detoxification and inflammatory signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis of CAF signatures, with citation supporting the functional characterization.

claim: ECM-myCAF S1 is associated with immunosuppressive microenvironment and pro-metastatic functions.
source: DE and MU were most strongly enriched in signatures of ECM-myCAF S1 – associated with immunosuppressive microenvironment and pro-metastatic functions (Kieffer et al., 2020) – and wound-healing myCAF S1 populations, while the adjacent stroma mainly showed signatures of normal fibroblasts, detox-iCAF S1 and IL-iCAF S1 populations, both characterized by detoxification and inflammatory signaling.
evidence: This characterization is supported by citation to Kieffer et al., 2020.

claim: Adjacent stroma mainly showed signatures of normal fibroblasts, detox-iCAF S1 and IL-iCAF S1 populations.
source: DE and MU were most strongly enriched in signatures of ECM-myCAF S1 – associated with immunosuppressive microenvironment and pro-metastatic functions (Kieffer et al., 2020) – and wound-healing myCAF S1 populations, while the adjacent stroma mainly showed signatures of normal fibroblasts, detox-iCAF S1 and IL-iCAF S1 populations, both characterized by detoxification and inflammatory signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis of CAF signatures.

claim: NR regions were enriched only in normal fibroblasts and detox-iCAF S1.
source: NR regions were enriched only in normal fibroblasts and detox-iCAF S1.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis of CAF signatures.

claim: The discriminative gradients between morphotypes were along the EMT and TNF-α signaling axes at one end, and the MYC and E2F targets at the other end.
source: When considering only the hallmark signatures (H collection), the discriminative gradients between the morphotypes (and NR and ST) were along the EMT and TNF-α signaling axes at one end, and the MYC and E2F targets at the other end (Table 1, Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis shown in Table 1 and Figure 3A.

claim: Desmoplastic and mucinous morphotypes shared active pathways involved in immune system response (TNF-α signaling via NF-κB, interferon gamma response, complement, IL2-STAT5 signaling).
source: Desmoplastic and mucinous shared active pathways involved in immune system response (TNF-α signaling via NF-κB, interferon gamma response, complement, IL2-STAT5 signaling), neoangiogenesis, and increased metastatic potential (EMT, coagulation, TGF-β, NF-kB, NOTCH, Apical junction).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: Desmoplastic and mucinous morphotypes shared active pathways involved in neoangiogenesis and increased metastatic potential (EMT, coagulation, TGF-β, NF-kB, NOTCH, Apical junction).
source: Desmoplastic and mucinous shared active pathways involved in immune system response (TNF-α signaling via NF-κB, interferon gamma response, complement, IL2-STAT5 signaling), neoangiogenesis, and increased metastatic potential (EMT, coagulation, TGF-β, NF-kB, NOTCH, Apical junction).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: CT and TB morphotypes had activated major pathways involved in proliferation processes (P53, MTORC 1, Myc targets, G2M checkpoint, Mitotic spindle, NOTCH signaling, Protein secretion).
source: At the other end of the spectrum, CT and TB morphotypes had activated major pathways involved in proliferation processes (P53, MTORC 1, Myc targets, G2M checkpoint, Mitotic spindle, NOTCH signaling, Protein secretion).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: TB morphotype shared with MU and DE active TGF-β signaling, apoptosis, and most pathways involved in immune system response.
source: In contrast with CT, TB morphotype shared with MU and DE active TGF-β signaling, apoptosis, and most pathways involved in immune system response.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: PP and SE morphotypes had activated MYC and E2F targets.
source: PP and SE morphotypes had activated MYC and E2F targets, with PP morphotype exhibiting downregulation of the KRAS signaling and upregulation of the WNT-β catenin signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: PP morphotype exhibited downregulation of the KRAS signaling and upregulation of the WNT-β catenin signaling.
source: PP and SE morphotypes had activated MYC and E2F targets, with PP morphotype exhibiting downregulation of the KRAS signaling and upregulation of the WNT-β catenin signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: All ST regions were predicted as CMS4.
source: All ST regions were predicted as CMS4, and 82.4% of NR regions as CMS3.
evidence: This is a finding from applying CMS classifier to the data.

claim: 82.4% of NR regions were predicted as CMS3.
source: All ST regions were predicted as CMS4, and 82.4% of NR regions as CMS3.
evidence: This is a finding from applying CMS classifier to the data.

claim: DE and MU were most often assigned to CMS4 (63.6% and 58.8%).
source: For the morphotypes, the predictions were more distributed across subtypes: DE and MU were most often assigned to CMS4 (63.6% and 58.8%), PP, SE, and CT to CMS2 (62.5%, 41.7% and 41.9%) and TB to CMS1 (80%; Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from applying CMS classifier to the data, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PP, SE, and CT were most often assigned to CMS2 (62.5%, 41.7% and 41.9%).
source: For the morphotypes, the predictions were more distributed across subtypes: DE and MU were most often assigned to CMS4 (63.6% and 58.8%), PP, SE, and CT to CMS2 (62.5%, 41.7% and 41.9%) and TB to CMS1 (80%; Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from applying CMS classifier to the data, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TB was most often assigned to CMS1 (80%).
source: For the morphotypes, the predictions were more distributed across subtypes: DE and MU were most often assigned to CMS4 (63.6% and 58.8%), PP, SE, and CT to CMS2 (62.5%, 41.7% and 41.9%) and TB to CMS1 (80%; Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from applying CMS classifier to the data, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: CMS heterogeneity was observed intra-tumoral, with regions within the same tumor section being assigned to different subtypes.
source: More importantly, this heterogeneity was also observed intra-tumoral, with regions within the same tumor section being assigned to different subtypes (Figures 4A and 5, Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing CMS assignments across regions within tumors, shown in Figures 4A and 5.

claim: Intrinsic molecular subtypes (iCMS2/3) were much more stable than CMS, with most morphotypes within a tumor sharing the same iCMS label.
source: In contrast, intrinsic molecular subtypes (iCMS2/3) were much more stable, most of the time all the morphotypes within a tumor sharing the same iCMS label (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and agreeing with the whole-tumor assignment.
evidence: This is a finding from applying iCMS classifier to the data, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: NR, MU, TB, and ST regions were classified most of the time as iCMS3 (100%, 94,4%, 71.4%, 66.7%).
source: NR, MU, TB, and ST regions were classified most of the time as iCMS3 (100%, 94,4%, 71.4%, 66.7%), while PP, CT and DE were predominantly classified as iCMS2 (77.8%, 70.3%, 66.7%).
evidence: This is a finding from applying iCMS classifier to the data.

claim: PP, CT and DE were predominantly classified as iCMS2 (77.8%, 70.3%, 66.7%).
source: NR, MU, TB, and ST regions were classified most of the time as iCMS3 (100%, 94,4%, 71.4%, 66.7%), while PP, CT and DE were predominantly classified as iCMS2 (77.8%, 70.3%, 66.7%).
evidence: This is a finding from applying iCMS classifier to the data.

claim: The serrated morphotype was almost equally assigned to each of the iCMSs (iCMS2: 58%, iCMS3:42%).
source: The serrated morphotype was almost equally assigned to each of the iCMSs (iCMS2: 58%, iCMS3:42%).
evidence: This is a finding from applying iCMS classifier to the data.

claim: Two prognostic signatures (Eschrich and Jorissen) reached statistical significance in their variation across morphotypes (Kruskal-Wallis's test: Eschrich p=0.0228, Jorissen p=0.00085).
source: The morphotypes generally differed in terms of score distributions, with two signatures reaching statistical significance (Kruskal-Wallis's test: Eschrich p=0.0228, Jorissen p=0.00085, Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from testing prognostic signatures across morphotypes, shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: Amplitude of differences between tumor regions and matched whole tumor for prognostic signatures was larger than 50% of the whole tumor score in some cases.
source: A more pronounced variability was observed when comparing tumor regions to matched whole tumor, with amplitude of the differences (region vs whole tumor) larger than 50% of the whole tumor score in some cases (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing regional and whole tumor prognostic scores, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MU morphotype showed predicted resistance to gefitinib.
source: The predicted resistance/sensitivity to different therapeutics varied across morphotypes: MU resistance to gefitinib; DE sensitivity to azaticidine, dasatinib, and aplidin, and resistance to tamoxifen and gefitinib; PP resistance to cantharidin, SE resistance to aplidin, CT sensitivity to alkylating agents (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from applying drug sensitivity signatures to the data, shown in Figure 6.

claim: DE morphotype showed sensitivity to azaticidine, dasatinib, and aplidin, and resistance to tamoxifen and gefitinib.
source: The predicted resistance/sensitivity to different therapeutics varied across morphotypes: MU resistance to gefitinib; DE sensitivity to azaticidine, dasatinib, and aplidin, and resistance to tamoxifen and gefitinib; PP resistance to cantharidin, SE resistance to aplidin, CT sensitivity to alkylating agents (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from applying drug sensitivity signatures to the data, shown in Figure 6.

claim: PP morphotype showed resistance to cantharidin.
source: The predicted resistance/sensitivity to different therapeutics varied across morphotypes: MU resistance to gefitinib; DE sensitivity to azaticidine, dasatinib, and aplidin, and resistance to tamoxifen and gefitinib; PP resistance to cantharidin, SE resistance to aplidin, CT sensitivity to alkylating agents (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from applying drug sensitivity signatures to the data, shown in Figure 6.

claim: SE morphotype showed resistance to aplidin.
source: The predicted resistance/sensitivity to different therapeutics varied across morphotypes: MU resistance to gefitinib; DE sensitivity to azaticidine, dasatinib, and aplidin, and resistance to tamoxifen and gefitinib; PP resistance to cantharidin, SE resistance to aplidin, CT sensitivity to alkylating agents (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from applying drug sensitivity signatures to the data, shown in Figure 6.

claim: CT morphotype showed sensitivity to alkylating agents.
source: The predicted resistance/sensitivity to different therapeutics varied across morphotypes: MU resistance to gefitinib; DE sensitivity to azaticidine, dasatinib, and aplidin, and resistance to tamoxifen and gefitinib; PP resistance to cantharidin, SE resistance to aplidin, CT sensitivity to alkylating agents (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from applying drug sensitivity signatures to the data, shown in Figure 6.

claim: Some supposedly sensitive tumors (based on whole tumor scoring) had regions of predicted resistance.
source: The differences were observed even within tumor (Figure 5), with some of the supposedly sensitive tumors (whole tumor scoring) having regions of predicted resistance (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing regional and whole tumor drug sensitivity predictions, shown in Figure 5 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: MU and DE morphotypes exhibited high score of genes up-regulated in colon fibroblast TGF-β signaling pathway and genes associated with high tumor stromal content.
source: MU and DE morphotypes (previously associated with CMS1 and CMS4, Budinska et al., 2013), as expected, exhibited high score of genes up-regulated in colon fibroblast TGF-β signaling pathway, genes associated with high tumor stromal content, CAFs and endothelial cells as well as pathways involved in immune system response.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis, with citation to previous work.

claim: The supportive stroma (ST) region had the complete panel of fibroblast tested, while DE and MU most notably missed the 'normal CAFs'.
source: The detailed analysis of CAFs in fibroblast-rich regions (DE, MU, and ST) based on signatures derived from single cell sequencing studies (Pelka et al., 2021; Kieffer et al., 2020) revealed some finer differences: the supportive stroma (ST) region had the complete panel of fibroblast tested, while DE and MU most notably missed the 'normal CAFs'.
evidence: This is a finding from CAF signature analysis, with citations to the source of signatures.

claim: The main difference between DE and MU was that DE was enriched in CAFs associated with inflammatory response (IL-iCAF).
source: The main difference between DE and MU appeared to be that former was enriched in CAFs associated with inflammatory response (IL-iCAF), all the other CAFs being present at similar levels.
evidence: This is a finding from CAF signature analysis.

claim: The poor prognosis associated with CMS4 could be explained by the stromal component.
source: Further, the poor prognostic associated with CMS4 could be explained by the stromal component: both (Roseweir et al., 2020) and (Ten Hoorn et al., 2022) agree that a high stromal invasion/desmoplastic reaction is prognostic of shorter time to relapse.
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to Roseweir et al., 2020 and Ten Hoorn et al., 2022.

claim: A high stromal invasion/desmoplastic reaction is prognostic of shorter time to relapse.
source: Further, the poor prognostic associated with CMS4 could be explained by the stromal component: both (Roseweir et al., 2020) and (Ten Hoorn et al., 2022) agree that a high stromal invasion/desmoplastic reaction is prognostic of shorter time to relapse.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Roseweir et al., 2020 and Ten Hoorn et al., 2022.

claim: CT morphotype was associated mainly with subtype B (vastly overlapping with CMS2) in Budinska et al., 2013.
source: CT morphotype represents a classic adenocarcinoma and is one of the most common morphologies. In our previous study (Budinska et al., 2013), this morphotype was associated mainly with subtype B (vastly overlapping with CMS2).
evidence: This is a reference to findings from a previous study by the authors.

claim: TB morphotype seems to be mostly representative of higher-grade tumors and was associated with CMS1.
source: TB morphotype seems to be mostly representative of higher-grade tumors and was associated with CMS1.
evidence: This is an observation from the current study.

claim: CT and TB showed significant enrichment of signatures of normal colon basal cells in contrast to NR.
source: In contrast to NR, CT and TB showed significant enrichment of signatures of normal colon basal cells.
evidence: This is a finding from gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: SE and PP morphologies may be indicative of a different oncologic pathway – the 'serrated pathway'.
source: SE and PP morphologies may be indicative of a different oncologic pathway – the 'serrated pathway' (De Palma et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citation to De Palma et al., 2019.

claim: SE and PP morphologies share common features like well to moderately differentiated, with low stromal content and crypt structure still preserved.
source: The two morphologies share common features like well to moderately differentiated, with low stromal content and crypt structure still preserved.
evidence: This is a histopathological observation.

claim: Both SE and PP were distributed similarly across molecular subtypes (both CMS and iCMS) and had similar activation of hallmark pathways.
source: From a molecular perspective, we found that both SE and PP were both distributed similarly across molecular subtypes (both CMS and iCMS) and had similar activation of hallmark pathways: EMT, IL2/STAT5, IL6/STAT3, KRAS signaling all being down-regulated, while MYC targets being up-regulated.
evidence: This is a finding from molecular subtype classification and pathway analysis.

claim: In SE and PP, EMT, IL2/STAT5, IL6/STAT3, KRAS signaling were all down-regulated, while MYC targets were up-regulated.
source: From a molecular perspective, we found that both SE and PP were both distributed similarly across molecular subtypes (both CMS and iCMS) and had similar activation of hallmark pathways: EMT, IL2/STAT5, IL6/STAT3, KRAS signaling all being down-regulated, while MYC targets being up-regulated.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis.

claim: DPYD gene variants are predictive of 5-fluoruracil toxicity in adjuvant colon cancer treatment.
source: At the other end of the list, very interestingly, we found significantly downregulated gene for dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPYD) gene – the variants of which are predictive of 5-fluoruracil toxicity in adjuvant colon cancer treatment (Lee et al., 2014), GLIPR2 which participates in positive regulation of ERK1/2 cascade and EMT transition (Kang et al., 2012b), or the HOXA9A gene, the overexpression of which was suggested to contribute to stem cell overpopulation responsible for development of CRC (Osmond et al., 2022) or the GLI3 gene – that participates in sonic hedgehog (Shh)-Gli-mediated tumorigenesis and the loss of Gli3 signaling was shown to initiate cell growth inhibition in colon cancer cells, while sensitizing colon cancer cells to treatment with anti-cancer agents (5-FU and bevacizumab) (Kang et al., 2012a).

claim: The whole tumor CMS class differed from at least one of the constituent morphological regions in about 60% of cases (11 out of 18).
source: In our collection, several cases were represented by several regions and an additional whole-tumor profile. Taking advantage of these matched samples, we investigated several molecular classifiers from an intra-tumor variability perspective as well. The CMS classification was less stable than iCMS, with whole tumor CMS class differing from at least one of the constituent morphological regions in about 60% of cases (11 out of 18, excluding cases in which CMS class was not predicted; see Figure 5).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing CMS assignments between whole tumor and regions, shown in Figure 5.

claim: All prognostic signatures varied with the morphological regions with some cases where morphotype scores exceeded corresponding whole tumor scores by more than 50%.

evidence: This is a finding from comparing prognostic signature scores across regions and whole tumor.

claim: In some cases, whole tumor-based predictions were too optimistic, with models failing to recognize higher risk cases.

claim: Prognostic and response to therapy signatures may predict more severe cases when applied to subregions than to the whole tumor.
source: Our analyses indicate that both prognostic and response to therapy signatures may predict more severe cases (shorter relapse free survival or resistance to therapy) when applied to subregions than to the whole tumor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of signatures across regions.

claim: Signature failure in real-world validation might be due to morphologically heterogeneous tumors needing several sampling locations.
